Maya / Rafael —

Thanks — I reviewed Novum's annotated PDF and drafted two alternative passages for Section 5 (Output / Productization). I attached a docx with tracked changes (RN-OrderForm-v3-redlines.docx). Summary below.

Option 1 (Preferred by Redwood): Perpetual, non-exclusive license- Novum receives a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, display and create derivative works of output generated by Redwood's Service when Novum supplies inputs (Prompts, Data) through the Order Form. This license expressly permits productization in Novum's SaaS offering. Redwood retains rights to use aggregated telemetry and service logs for operations and to improve models, subject to the customer's training opt-out below.

Option 2 (Narrow assignment trigger): Assignment only if customer provides identified training artifacts- If Novum elects to transfer to Redwood exclusive model weights or other training artifacts and those artifacts are accepted by Redwood in writing as a customer-provided trained artifact, then ownership of the resulting derivative model (but not Redwood's underlying model code) may be assigned to Novum on mutually agreeable terms and documented in an Exhibit (including escrow provisions).

Training / Feedback handling (proposed wording):
- Default: Redwood does not ingest customer-provided data for model training unless Novum opts in via the Order Form and signs the training consent Exhibit.
- Evidence: For customers who opt-out, Redwood will provide a monthly ingestion report and a signed attestation that no customer data was used in training. For customers who opt-in, we capture ingestion receipts and can provide the list of accepted artifacts on request.

Telemetry / Auditing (operational evidence we can deliver):
- Ingestion receipts (timestamped file IDs)
- Service-level usage logs (token-level timestamps, per-session hashes) retained for 90 days by default (longer retention available as an add-on)
- Exportable audit CSV for all calls tied to the Account ID for the SOW period

Open items for negotiation:
- Whether Novum requires assignment language in the MSA or if the license + Exhibit approach is sufficient for procurement.
- Escrow mechanics and acceptance criteria for any assigned trained artifacts.

Next steps: Rafael — if Novum agrees in principle to Option 1 with the Exhibit approach for assignment triggers, I suggest we finalize the license text and circulate to Novum legal for a single pass. If they insist on assignment in MSA, we will need procurement-level approval and a proposed escrow template.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Procurement
Redwood Inference
